title: A sensational seat and gripping graffiti – readers’ best photographs

author: Jessica Murray  and Neha Gohil
description:
Labour’s plan to get young unemployed people into work involves overhaul of welfare support, but for those with disabilities, specialist help is crucial

When Rory Bowman finished school he joined the cohort of almost a million Neets – young people not in education, employment or training – around the country.

The 21-year-old has autism and said he was exhausted after struggling for support in mainstream education for years. He didn’t think he could manage university, but couldn’t find a job or training that would accommodate his neurodivergence.

Continue reading...
title: ‘They learn the job doing the job’: the project helping UK’s Neets into work

author: Timothy Garton Ash
description:
The PM’s first big speech on the UK and Europe was cautious and disappointing. Don’t expect any great leaps towards a new deal

Ever since Andy Burnham became the British prime minister this summer, people all over Europe have been asking me one question: “Will the UK rejoin the EU?” Sometimes they add: “And if so, when?” None of the intermediate options between the current hard Brexit and Brejoin are of any interest at all to most other Europeans.

Measured against these great expectations, Burnham’s first big speech on Britain and Europe, delivered on Monday evening amid all the pomp and circumstance the City of London could furnish, must be considered a disappointment. It was both a cautious and a curiously old-fashioned speech.
title: Hoping for Britain to rejoin the EU with Andy Burnham? You may be waiting a long time | Timothy Garton Ash

author: Kate Wyver
description:
A radical new take on Virginia Woolf’s modernist classic includes a Berlin ketamine binge, a ‘goon cave’ and an all-trans cast. The manifesto? To ‘desecrate’ expectations

As Orlando’s on a comedown after a ket-heavy night out in Berlin, surrounded by a group of sharp-tongued trans sex workers, Charli Cowgill and Laurie Ward pause the read-through. The scene is new and “it’s feeling a little safe,” Ward says, drumming the table. “How can we make it riskier?”

Cowgill and Ward are piss/CARNATION, a theatre-making duo creating fearless, messy and intellectually rigorous work. Audience spit was collected and thrown in their first production, 52 Monologues for Young Transsexuals, a show that collated trans women’s experiences of men and sex work. Ugly Sisters, the pair’s riotous follow-up, relived a brief encounter between a trans woman and Germaine Greer who wrote a caustic
title: ‘Dolls deserve complex roles’: the trans theatre troupe turning Orlando into a ‘porno-biography’

author: Press Association
description:
Former England footballer reveals that the issues he faced occurred at the height of his Manchester United career

Wayne Rooney has revealed there was a period in his Manchester United career where he contemplated taking his own life. The former England striker said that, even as he flourished on the pitch, he was struggling with his mental health off it, despite being newly married and a dad to his eldest child, Kai.

He said he would spend two days at a time drinking at home and, he told the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, at his lowest point considered taking his own life. “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” Rooney said. “Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.
title: Wayne Rooney says he contemplated taking own life during playing career

author: Ed Aarons
description:
• Storey made 501 appearances for Arsenal from 1965

  • He got 19 England caps and finished career at Fulham

Arsenal have paid tribute to Peter Storey, a key member of their 1971 Double-winning team, after the death of the former England midfielder at the age of 81.

Storey was part of the Bertie Mee team that secured the First Division title and FA Cup in a season that remains one of the most celebrated in Arsenal’s history and played 501 times for the club. That places him eighth on their appearances list.

Continue reading...
title: Peter Storey, Arsenal Double winner and England international, dies aged 81

author: Arwa Mahdawi
description:
Now the vice-president’s luck is turning, he seems reluctant to commit himself to the next presidential race – and I, for one, hate to see it

How do you think history will remember JD Vance? As the first vice-president to spark a vigorous debate about their eyeliner routine? As one of the last public figures to see Pope Francis alive? As the only politician in US history to have been the subject of a rumour about sexual relations with a couch (even though it was unfounded)?

I have no idea. But it seems increasingly unlikely he will be remembered as the 48th president of the US. After Maga’s midterm thrashing, Vance’s political future doesn’t look as b
title: Should JD Vance run for president? I say go for it, habibi! | Arwa Mahdawi

author: Agencies
description:
• Former world No 1 last competed at the Open in 2024

  • Woods was arrested on DUI charge earlier this year

Tiger Woods will make ⁠his long-awaited return to competitive golf at the Hero World Challenge next month at the unofficial event he hosts in the Bahamas.

His decision was posted on Instagram, with Woods joining the 20-man field along with Rickie Fowler and 2019 US Open champion Gary Woodland. The Hero World Challenge takes place in New Providence, Bahamas, from 3 to 6 December.

Continue reading...
title: Tiger Woods to make golf return after two years at Hero World Challenge

author: Marcela Mora y Araujo
description:
A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation

“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.

The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match its
title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Home Office changes policy after legal challenge over case of care worker scammed out of £22,000

Migrant workers who are financially exploited can now be considered victims of modern slavery, after a legal challenge by a care worker who was scammed out of £22,000 to pay an agent for a job in the UK that did not exist.

The care worker, Ali*, from Pakistan, was put in contact with an agent who told him he could organise a certificate of sponsorship for him to work in a UK care home. The agent was recommended by a friend who said he had been helped to secure a UK care job.

Continue reading...
title: Scammed migrant workers in UK to be considered possible victims of modern slavery

author: Jessica Salter
description:
From grippy socks and posh condiments to beautiful stationery and accessories, these affordable Christmas presents are anything but naff

• The best Christmas gifts for 2026

Secret Santa is an amazing concept to reduce the amount of gifts you feel obliged to buy, but I find it can result in quite a bit of tat. Resist the urge to buy a joke gift – often instant landfill – and use your budget to get your recipient something useful, or that feels quite treat-y.

I’m assuming for this guide that the rules of Secret Santa are that you know who your recipient is – they just don’t know who the gift is from. That is helpful as you can tailor it to their tastes and hobbies. If it’s blind both ways, food is always well received, and socks – while a Christmas cliche – are something everyone wants a new pair of (just get the best you can afford, not, as one
title: The 45 best Secret Santa gifts in the UK for £15 or less – tried and tested for 2026

author: Helena Horton
description:
Exclusive: Parents of Chloe Moffat urge employers to treat staff facing allegations in a kinder, more human way

The parents of a Treasury worker who took her own life last year have launched a policy that directs employers to treat staff in a kinder and more commonsense way, and are asking HR departments across the country to adopt it.

Chloe Moffat’s parents also said the government department plans to plant a memorial garden in her honour at its Horse Guards Road offices.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Chloe’s policy’ aims to prevent repeat of case of Treasury worker who took her own life

author: Blake Montgomery
description:
Huang’s exit sharpens debate over US stance towards Beijing; and as outages increase, do you get the feeling nothing works?

  • This was originally published in TechScape, a newsletter about how technology shapes our lives. Sign up to receive it here.

Hello, and welcome to TechScape. I’m your host, Blake Montgomery, US tech editor at the Guardian, writing to you from a plane back from Web Summit in Lisbon. Today in tech, we’re discussing the implications of Jensen Huang’s ouster, and the recent spate of failures in critical infrastructure in everything from Microsoft Outlook accounts to air traffic control to copper wires in routers.

Continue reading...
title: Jensen Huang’s departure as Nvidia CEO becomes a political proxy war

author: Kalyeena Makortoff Banking correspondent
description:
International investigation using trove of leaked internal data allegedly shows German bank overlooked compliance concerns to safeguard profits

Deutsche Bank reportedly dismissed warnings about its dealings with risky clients, including high-profile Russian oligarchs, to protect profits, the findings of an investigation into a trove of leaked bank documents indicate.

A leak of 15m internal files is reported to show that the troubled German bank repeatedly ignored concerns by its compliance officers about its risk-taking, despite having already been caught being used to launder billions of dollars for Russian criminals, spies and oligarchs between 2010 and 2015.

Continue reading...
title: Deutsche Bank dismissed warnings about dealings with risky clients, reports claim

author: Miatta Fahnbulleh
description:
I am at Cop 31 – concerned about the crisis around the world, but mindful that voters want jobs, warmer homes and cheaper prices

  • Miatta Fahnbulleh is the UK secretary of state for energy security and net zero

In this cold weather, it is easy to forget that Britain has just been through its hottest summer on record, part of our new reality as the climate crisis reaches our doorstep. For millions around the world, the consequences have already been more devastating for the communities that did the least to cause this crisis.

That is the backdrop to Cop31 in Antalya, Turkey, where I arrive on Tuesday as the UK’s chief negotiator. As I have prepared for these negotiations, I’ve been reflecting on the gap between the science and the political debate in Britain. Early predictions by the Met Office indicate that 2027 will surpass 2024 as the hottest year on record globally as El Niño rips
title: Where do people want to see Britain’s climate action plan working? On their own doorstep | Miatta Fahnbulleh

author: Tom Garry
description:
• Head coach excited by ‘high potential’ of players

  • Striker Goodwin and keeper Cox in squad for first time

Sarina Wiegman says the potential in England’s emerging young players helped convince her to extend her contract until the end of 2029’s European Championship.

The Lionesses head coach, whose previous deal was due to expire next year, gave first senior call-ups to the striker Isobel Goodwin and goalkeeper Katie Cox on Tuesday as she named her squad for December’s two-leg World Cup qualifying playoff against Ukraine.

Continue reading...
title: Wiegman cites young talent as key to new England deal after calling up Goodwin

author: Hilary Osborne
description:
Stock market debut of Claude AI chatbot maker is expected to be one of the biggest flotations in history

The technology company Anthropic is heading for a blockbuster stock market listing this week in what is slated to be one of the largest debuts in history.

The company is a leader in artificial intelligence, and is best known for its chatbot Claude. The float, which is expected to value the business at $1.4tn (£1tn), comes at a volatile time for tech stocks, yet it has been reported that the shares could be six times oversubscribed.

Continue reading...
title: Anthropic IPO: how can I buy shares, and is it worth it?

author: Anna Berrill
description:
Direct the heat and minimise the moisture to save your pastry from a saturated bottom, says our panel of pie pros

Why does the pastry base of my apple pie always come out soggy? What am I doing wrong?
Sophie, by email
“The very first thing I would say is that Sophie has got to look at her filling, and how wet it is,” says Calum Franklin, author of The Modern Pie Maker and all-round pie Yoda. “Apples contain quite a lot of water already, so you don’t generally need to add any extra liquid to the filling.” Instead, he’d simply cook the apples with sugar: “Just let them break down.”

That said, Sophie could always consider including some sort of barrier, too, says Dee Rettali, co-founder of Fortitude Bakehouse in London: “My mother was an amazing baker, and
title: Help! Why does my apple pie always have a soggy base? | Kitchen aide

author: Lewis Gordon
description:
PC; Forward Instinct
This irreverent stealth game depicts Samuel’s lonely life robbing garish, midwestern abodes – it’s a Shameless way to make a living

For many people, McMansions are an eyesore, but for the protagonist of Keepsake County, a renowned burglar, they are an enticing opportunity. Prowling at purple-hued dusk, this unfussy thief is just as likely to steal a half-eaten slice of pizza or a naff ceramic ornament as he is an expensive set of golf clubs. It’s a sad, desperate way to make a living, a sense compounded by what this fledgling kleptomaniac carries his loot away in: a plastic shopping bag.

Countless works have taken us to breadline America, from classic novel East of Eden to acclaimed TV crime drama Mare of Easttown. But Keepsake County is no prestige examination of the economic underbelly of the US. Rather, it is a stealing simulator with eccentric Adult Swim-style art and a darkly absurdist sense of humour that is expressed in it
title: Keepsake County review – eccentric stealing simulator with a social conscience

author: Frances Ryan
description:
The long-awaited plan to address youth unemployment in the UK has positive aspects, but it will cause huge anxiety for young people with disabilities

Continue reading...
title: Age instead of need drives Alan Milburn’s new reforms. Welcome to the two-tier welfare state | Frances Ryan

author: Gabrielle Canon in Antalya
description:
The 120-strong America Is All In group are trying to ensure that the US won’t remained sidelined at the climate talks for very much longer. Plus: wild oysters are back in Scotland and a super El Niño looms over Cop

• Don’t get Down to Earth delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

The final week of Cop31 is in full swing, with just four days left to set a broad range of climate commitments into concrete action. I am on the ground at this year’s UN annual climate summit, where thousands of world leaders, businesses, nonprofits and scientists have converged in Antalya, Turkey, and there’s a lot left to do as the clock ticks down.

“Nearly 200 countries are working through 165 mandates,” executive secretary Simon Stiell told reporters at the midpoint on Saturday, pushing for a swift move to the hardest issues
title: ‘We are all in’: the Democrats trying to turn round the US’s reputation at Cop31

author: Olivia McEwan
description:
Royal Academy, London
The modernist collector once ran a gallery in London – but from this confusing exhibition, it’s hard to tell what exactly was once in there

Peggy Guggenheim, art enthusiast and socialite born into a wealthy New York family, was often photographed outside her palazzo in Venice with a handbag dog and outré sunglasses. The Peggy Guggenheim Collection as we now know it, however, was nearly not in her Venice palazzo but London, evidenced by a short-lived and largely overlooked period between January 1938 and June 1939 when she ran Guggenheim Jeune in Cork Street. This exhibition posits that this initial gallery’s activities were far more influential in the shaping of contemporary art than previo
title: ‘She set out to buy a painting a day’: on the trail of Peggy Guggenheim’s legendary shopping spree

author: Tom Ambrose
description:
Challenger nears 50% of the ballot to secure victory in final midterms contest

  • Protests greet Trump on Asia visit – follow live

  • Sign up for US Breaking News email

The Democrats’ midterm “blue wave” wins gave them strong majorities in both chambers of Congress, new governors’ mansions and power in some unexpected places.

Voters dealt a stunning rebuke to Donald Trump – and his ruthless deportation
title: Democrats’ Peltola ahead as counting nears end in Alaska Senate race – US politics live

description:
The Guardian’s picture editors select photographs from around the world

Continue reading...
title: Anti-Trump protests in Manila and a red crab migration: photos of the day – Tuesday

author: Luca Cesari
description:
Spag bol carries my city’s name all over the world – to the embarrassment of restaurants in Bologna

In Bologna, spaghetti bolognese does not exist. You’ll find it on menus in London and Sydney, in British school canteens and in jars on supermarket shelves across half the world, but not in the city that lent it its name. Order it in a trattoria beneath the Two Towers and at best you get a pitying smile. More often you’ll be brought a plate of tagliatelle, with a short lesson in local history on the side.

Few of the Italian dishes famous abroad carry the name of a city. Every so often the argument flares up again over where pizza, carbonara or
title: A heretical outrage: why Italians disown spaghetti bolognese

author: Stevie Chick
description:
The Scottish quartet existed for just three years at the turn of the millennium. But after Frank Ocean and TikTok thrilled to Sue Tompkins’ unique vocals, they’re back. They explain their fears about ‘spoiling the joy’

‘I’m excited, I’m scared, I’m anxious – that bubbling feeling, like when you’re on a rollercoaster, at the very top, just before the big drop.”

On a drizzly afternoon in July, huddled with her three bandmates in the cramped cupboard that’s the dressing room of Glasgow venue Mono, Sue Tompkins is managing her feelings ahead of her first proper gig with Life Without Buildings in almost a quarter of a century. “Everybody coming is invited, it’s secret, nobody paid much to get in, the profits are going to charity,” adds guitarist Robert Dallas Gray, sat beside her, as much to steady his own nerves as to explain the circumstances of tonight’s show. “I hope people aren’t looking at it like we’re fucking entertainers.”
title: They’re one of the UK’s greatest cult bands – who swore they’d never reunite. What brought Life Without Buildings back together?

author: Rowan Glass in Poyeni, Peru
description:
Decades after Lima armed them to fight Shining Path rebels, the Asháninka are still defending their Amazon rainforest, but now against drug traffickers – and without any help

Shielding his eyes from the tropical sun, Irmeo Sánchez Gómez – better known by his nom de guerre, Kiri – pointed up at a weathered shed on top of a hill, a few frayed sandbags piled at its base. Beyond it, the Tambo River snaked through Peru’s Amazonian rainforest.

“When the terrorists came,” Kiri says, “they would shoot up at us from the riverbank. Without guns of our own, we defended ourselves with bows and arrows. Later, the army gave us guns and built these defences.”

Continue reading...
title: Bows and old guns: Indigenous militias left to fight Peru’s cocaine gangs alone

author: Chelsey Sharpe, as told to Suneet Gill
description:
She set off for home in bright sunshine in British Columbia, Canada. Then the rains came – and the mud. This is Chelsey Sharpe’s story

Location: Agassiz, Canada

Disaster: Southern British Columbia floods, 2021

In 2021, Chelsey Sharpe was working part-time as a yoga instructor when a mudslide swept her car off the highway. Climate change made the heavy rains behind that mudslide and the 2021 floods across southern British Columbia more likely.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The landslide hit the side of my car. I heard screaming, and realised it was me’ – This is climate breakdown

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Former minister’s 278-page report calls for changes to employment regulations, education, healthcare and benefits

  • Business live – latest updates

  • Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts

  • Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on young people

Five months on from a first report detailing the growing crisis of young people who are not in education, employm
title: Neet ideas: what’s in Alan Milburn’s report on young people not in education, employment or training?

author: Lauren MacDougall (now) and Ajit Niranjan and Fiona Harvey (later)
description:
The Guardian’s environment editor Fiona Harvey and Europe environment correspondent Ajit Niranjan will answer your questions on Cop31, the draft deal on fossil fuels, the fight over climate finance and what overshooting 1.5C means for the world.

The Cop31 climate summit in Antalya is in its final days, and negotiators are fighting over a first draft of the deal.

It calls for “accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels, including through the immediate transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems”, and for tripling adaptation finance for poorer countries. But with the world heading past the 1.5C limit and countries deeply divided over finance, adaptation and the “just transition”, can Cop31 deliver anything that matters?

Continue reading...
title: What do you want to know about the Cop31 climate talks? Ask Fiona Harvey and Ajit Niranjan

author: Julia Kollewe
description:
Retailer’s British boss says John Healey ‘missed opportunity to back retailers’ in October’s budget

  • Business live – latest updates

Ikea has ditched some planned store openings in the UK blaming the cost of business taxes, which it said were the highest in Europe.

As its annual UK sales little more than flatlined at the Swedish flatpack furniture retailer, its UK boss, David McCabe, said: “There are locations where we were planning to open a new unit, and those plans have been abandoned due to the cost that we experience and the complexity within the market.

Continue reading...
title: Ikea ditches plans for new UK stores, blaming high business taxes

author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
description:
Major tours by the likes of Oasis helped make 2025 a lucrative year, with music export revenue reaching £4.8bn

Major tours by Oasis, Robbie Williams and Dua Lipa, as well as hit albums by the likes of Olivia Dean, have helped to push the UK music industry to record revenues.

But there are concerns over a widening gulf in income between A-listers such as these, and the less well-known artists that form the bulk of the UK’s music community.

Continue reading...
title: UK music industry hits record high of £8.4bn – but are working musicians being left behind?

author: Sidney Blumenthal
description:
Horowitz, who swung from the far left to the far right, sought total political warfare against institutions and immigration

Stephen Miller has risen to the top of the White House in the downdraft of Donald Trump’s abject defeat in the midterm elections. It is no irony to Trump that he has elevated Miller as his ideal bullying enforcer only after Trump’s own thorough repudiation. Appointing Miller is Trump’s denial that he is the worst thing he could possibly imagine: a loser.

Trump has no more time for adults in the room who might want to negotiate with the new powers-that-be in the Congress. He has searched his soul, as he explained in his interview on 60 Minutes, entertaining his wish to ascend to heaven.

Continue reading...
title: How the rightwing operative David Horowitz shaped Stephen Miller | Sidney Blumenthal

author: Lee Escobedo
description:
This month, the league rightly honors veterans across the US. But little is mentioned about the death tolls, or the reasons behind our wars

My mom taught me to thank veterans. Whenever we saw someone in a veterans hat, she set the example. Nobody in her family served, but my paternal grandfather fought in the Pacific in the second world war, and she was always grateful to hear his stories, even the repeats.

It’s one of the things she gave me that I held on to, even in my worst years. The anger I’ve carried about the unjust wars of my lifetime – Afghanistan, Iraq and now Iran – never targeted the people sent to fight them.

Continue reading...
title: The NFL’s Salute to Service honors the military – and leaves out the realities of war | Lee Escobedo

author: Jim Farber
description:
Beloved for his savage takedowns and rhapsodic raves, the legendary Village Voice reviewer opens up in a candid new documentary

Rows and rows of CDs, albums, cassettes and books creak and groan on shelves that snake around the walls and choke the halls of an apartment in New York City’s East Village. The clutter that sprawls through its rooms is so dense it suggests the twistiest parts of a Moroccan medina or a warren no self-respecting rabbit would allow. Buried amid the muddle is a man hunched over a computer keyboard, clacking out words meant to make sense of all the sounds that this physical media holds.

Welcome to the lair of Robert Christgau, the self-declared “Dean of American Rock Critics”, as seen in a new documentary provocatively titled The Last Critic. “Bob is someone who has probably listened to more music, and published more words about music, than anyone to walk the face of the earth, and he’s still doing
title: ‘Mick Jagger should fold up his penis and go home’: the caustic genius of music critic Robert Christgau

author: Cath Clarke
description:
Poh Si Teng’s powerful documentary follows three doctors from the US who sign up to volunteer at the Nasser hospital

This is the latest documentary about medics travelling to Palestine to treat civilian casualties; it’s a powerful, angry film, in a state of despair at the scale of suffering and devastation. A sliver of hope is the trio of doctors it profiles, individuals acting on their conscience. (The same can be said of director Poh Si Teng, who quit her job at ABC News and cashed in her savings to get the documentary off the ground.) It follows three American doctors who sign up to volunteer at the Nasser hospital in southern Gaza in early 2025 – though one of the trio, Thaer Ahmad, an ER doctor of Palestinian heritage from Chicago, is refused entry the night before they enter Gaza.

His colleagues, Dr Feroze Sidhwa, a trauma surgeon, and Dr Mark Perlmutter, a Jewish-American orthopae
title: American Doctor review – medics put their lives on the line in Gaza amid the carnage

author: Zoe Williams
description:
Intrigued by an unusual recipe for spinach tacos, I followed the instructions, but was left with a soggy, inedible mess. It turns out there are a lot of made-up meals out there

I can’t tell you when my Instagram algorithm changed, from – this is embarrassing, but what the hell – buff guys trying to exercise and being interrupted by a Staffordshire bull terrier who wants to help them exercise, to cooking videos, but it has. I now get endless food content, following the same format: a millennial has 20 minutes to make dinner for his or her beloved (it’s very gender neutral), and launches into some unlikely techniques. He might shove a load of chicken into a cake tin, sprinkle mismatched spices all over, bake it, then slice it, as if it were a cake. Or she might cook tagliatelle in a pan of milk and salmon. This is not how it’s done, I think, as I watch all the way to the end, and then am astonished to be fed yet more weird food content.

Drawn with an almost zombified lack
title: I got scammed on Instagram – and it led to a truly disgusting dinner | Zoe Williams

author: Alexandra Villarreal in New York
description:
Despite House and Senate majorities, Democrats face a battle to enact legislation – but they have the power to conduct tough new oversight

The Democrats’ midterm “blue wave” wins gave them strong majorities in both chambers of Congress, new governors’ mansions and power in some unexpected places. Voters dealt a stunning rebuke to Donald Trump – and his ruthless deportation campaign and violent ICE raids across the country were among the key issues that cost Republicans support. But what will Democrats do about the immigration cr
title: What do Democrats’ sweeping midterm wins mean for Trump’s ICE crackdown?

author: Alan Martin
description:
Tech on its last legs? Refurbished can be the cheaper, greener option. Here’s how to choose well and avoid the pitfalls

• How to make your phone last longer

Even if you do your best to avoid it, it’s hard to escape the noise of retailers offering implausible-seeming Black Friday discounts on desirable technology. What they won’t be so keen to highlight is the huge environmental cost that comes from feeding the capitalist beast year on year, given what an obvious sales vibe-killer it would be.

While the best approach for the planet is to opt out completely and observe the alternative holiday of Buy Nothing Day instead, such an approach can prove self-defeating for your finances in the long term. If you
title: Don’t buy new tech this Black Friday: expert tips for buying refurbished phones and laptops

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Move is designed to hinder building of more illegal settlements, which Foreign Office says Israel has ‘refused to clamp down on’

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Ed Miliband has announced the first set of sanctions against Israeli companies planning to build illegal settlements in the West Bank, after he pledged to try to prevent settlements that destroy the chances of a two-state solution.

The UK foreign secretary also announced he was placing sanctions on a rightwing activist Israeli group involved in trying to block aid into Gaza as recently as last month.

Continue reading...
title: Ed Miliband announces first sanctions on Israeli firms working in West Bank

author: Ali Martin in Hobart
description:
Wicketkeeper-batter could have represented Australia but was destined to play for his country of birth after watching the 2010-11 Ashes at 10

In an era of sardine tin schedules and franchise teams hoping to turn heads, it was refreshing to hear Jordan Cox at the beautiful Bellerive Oval and state how desperate he is to play for England as much as is humanly possible.

When the squads for this Australia tour were being discussed, the selector Marcus North gave the wicketkeeper-batter the option to sit out the Twenty20 leg before taking on South Africa’s imposing Test attack next month. Cox, recently handed a two-year central contract after a breakout summer, was having none of it.

Continue reading...
title: Why Jordan Cox refuses to take a breather: ‘If England want me, I’ll be there’

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Mowbray confirms he has had to ‘step back from my role’

  • Rovers are currently 13th in the Championship table

The Blackburn Rovers head coach Tony Mowbray has stood down from his role due to illness.

“Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role,” said Mowbray, whose team are 13th in the Championship. “I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

More details soon …

Continue reading...
title: Blackburn Rovers head coach Tony Mowbray steps down due to health issues

author: Graeme Wearden
description:
Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news

  • Apec and Asean summits live: protests await Trump in Manila, as Xi greets leaders in Shenzhen

China has threatened to retaliate against the US after Washington tightened restrictions on remote access to AI chips and servers.

At a press conference on Tuesday, China’s foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing would take “necessary measures” to safeguard its own interests, saying:

“The US has repeatedly overstretched the concept of national security, abused export controls and even interfered in China’s normal trade and technological cooperation with other countries, unjustifiably suppressing the development of China’s high-tech industries.”

“This is the wors
title: China vows to take ‘necessary measures’ against US AI chip restrictions, as investors brace for Nvidia’s results – business live

author: Helen Pidd
description:
Catherine Dobson calls for exception to England and Wales early release scheme for police who abuse position of trust

  • ‘He’s a master manipulator’: one woman’s fight against her abuser’s early release | Podcast

A woman who was coercively controlled by her “master manipulator” partner, who was a police officer, says she is frightened and angry to have learned he will be released early after serving just a third of his sentence.

Michael Harvey worked as a detective in Lancashire police’s sexual offenders management unit when he met Catherine Dobson, using the police database to track her movements after a chance encounter in a supermarket.

Continue reading...<
title: ‘Master manipulator’ police officer should not be released early from UK prison, says ex-partner

author: Ben Fisher
description:
Midfielder’s under-21s winner eclipsed Jude Bellingham’s mark and there was other talent to admire against France

There may have been an Mbappé on the pitch – Ethan, the younger brother of Kylian, with whom he shares a near-identical gait – but by the end there was only one precocious talent on the lips of those watching England overcome France in their under-21s clash. Max Dowman had done it again, lighting up another game, this time in filthy conditions at Ashton Gate. It was fitting he had the final say in a 3-2 win. The noise that accompanied his match-winning goal? Well, beyond the palpable excitement in the stands in Bristol, that would be the sound of the teenager sending yet another record tumbling.

Which one takes your fancy? Take your pick. At 14, playing for Arsenal’s under-19s, he became the Uefa Youth League’s youngest goalscorer. This time last year, after taking to the field at Slavia Prague aged 15 and 308 days, Dowman became the youngest player to feat
title: Max Dowman shines in England colours and sends another record tumbling

author: Eromo Egbejule west Africa correspondent
description:
Ban on illegal artisanal mining triggers mass exodus and diplomatic tensions with neighbouring Sahel states

In the border town of Kourémalé, split between Guinea and Mali, thousands of families have been trudging across the frontier over the past week after a sudden ban on illegal artisanal mining triggered a wave of displacement and a regional diplomatic dispute.

Some, like Seydou Traore, a miner in his 30s from Burkina Faso, made the 78-mile trek from Kourémalé to Ouezzindougou, farther inward. Last week, he gathered a small bundle of his belongings and fled Guinea after security forces ordered him and fellow miners to leave.

Continue reading...
title: Chaos as crackdown on illegal mining in Guinea causes wave of regional displacement

author: Jonathan Jones
description:
National Gallery, London
Bringing together all the pioneering master’s portraits for the first time reveals the way he clinically preserved monsters, merchants – even his wife – like flies in amber

The stubble is tiny yet silver-sharp on the chin of an unknown old man whom Jan van Eyck painted in oils 600 years ago: so long after both are dead you can still see this bloke needs a shave. The hairs on top of his head are just as miraculously caught, varying individually in paleness and lankness. You feast your eyes on the sagging skin of his throat with its overhangs and shady gulleys like a rock formation. He is a wonder, a freak of nature and yet a perfectly ordinary person. So are we all banal and marvellous, mundane and impossible, suggests Van Eyck.

The National Gallery has created a jewel box of a show bringing together all Van Eyck’s portraits as we define them – a painting of a person for its own sake. Yet portraitist was a long way from being
title: Van Eyck: The Portraits review – a jewel box of phenomenal death-defeating paintings

author: Susanna Rustin
description:
Sarah Blaffer Hrdy unpicked Darwinian sexism to rewrite the story of evolution. Now, she’s turned her attention to the nature of fatherhood

‘Spit here, dear,” Sarah Blaffer Hrdy said to her husband, Dan, handing him a vial when he arrived in New York after the birth of the couple’s first grandchild. It was 2014 and Hrdy was conducting an experiment. Having recorded a 63% jump in oxytocin in her saliva after spending hours cuddling the baby, she wanted to find out if something similar would happen to his hormones.

It did, although it took a day longer. In her latest book, Father Time: A Natural History of Men and Babies, Hrdy records with justified pride that “this was the first time anyone had demonstrated a bump in oxytocin levels among doting grandparents”.
title: Would more hands-on dads create a more peaceful world? This pioneering scientist thinks so

author: Bryan Armen Graham
description:
As Sylvester Stallone’s Oscar-winning drama celebrates its 50th anniversary, I Play Rocky helps to further turn the boxing hero into the stuff of legend

The story behind the making of Rocky has always sounded uncannily like Rocky itself. An unknown with an improbable dream, a skeptical establishment and a refusal to accept the odds: Sylvester Stallone’s real-life struggle to crack the industry and bring his breakthrough film to the screen contained all the elements of the underdog story he sought to tell. Now, half a century later, Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky has crafted those parallels into a crowd-pleasing yarn of its own.

It’s an extraordinary afterlife for a modest boxing flick that became the highest-grossing film of 1976 on a $1m budget and won the Oscar for best picture over one of the most stacked fields in history. Yet its greatest achievement may be the durability
title: Rocky is Philadelphia’s founding myth – and 50 years later, we’re still telling it

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Hilary Cass says draft bill is having ‘chilling effect’ on healthcare professionals and could pose a risk to parents

The expert behind a major review into children’s gender services has said she can no longer support proposed legislation to ban conversion practices related to sexual orientation and transgender identity.

Hilary Cass, a paediatrician who now sits in the House of Lords, initially indicated her support when the conversion practices bill was announced in the summer. However, she has now said the proposed ban is having a “chilling effect” on healthcare professionals and could pose a risk to parents.

Continue reading...
title: Expert behind NHS children’s gender services review says she cannot back conversion practices ban

author: Robert Kitson
description:
After their seismic defeat by Wales, New Zealand face the prospect of history repeating itself in unwanted ways

They still talk about the last – and only – time the All Blacks have contrived to lose twice in succession to England. Back in 2002-03, as now, there was a Rugby World Cup looming in Australia and New Zealand had no shortage of quality players. “There is so much talent in New Zealand that, if they don’t win the World Cup, there should be an inquiry,” opined Steve Hansen, Wales’s head coach at the time, ahead of England’s fateful visit to Wellington in the summer of 2003.

There’s a fresh inquiry under way now even before the All Blacks trot out of the Twickenham tunnel this weekend for the 48th meeting between the two nations. While Saturday’s 35-28 defeat to Wales ended a 73-year wait from a home perspective it has inevitably precipitated plenty of d
title: The Breakdown | Rattled All Blacks face rare twin threat as England eye back-to-back scalps

author: Ed Aarons
description:
By supporting the non-profit BigShoe, the Arsenal forward has earned deserved plaudits for his social conscience

Valerie Fiesser will never forget her surprise when Bukayo Saka contacted her out of the blue, asking whether he could help support a project in Nigeria in 2022. “I remember thinking: ‘Is this really Bukayo writing us an email?’” says the president of BigShoe, a non-profit organisation based in Frankfurt that has helped more than 10,000 children worldwide. “But that’s how he is. He’s always asking what more we can do.”

Four years on from that unexpected email, Fiesser was given the secret task of reaching out for a letter for Saka to read from the podium when he was presented with the Sócrates award at last month’s Ballon d’Or ceremony in London for his humanitarian work. She got the words from Byiringiro, a 14-year-old from Rwanda who ha
title: ‘He wants to change lives’: the story behind Bukayo Saka’s Sócrates award

author: Donna Ferguson. Photographs by Urszula Sołtys for the Guardian
description:
Farmers are utilising science and nature to help orchards adapt and thrive in the face of shifting temperatures, rainfall and pests

On Myrtle Farm in Somerset, there are thousands of apple trees laid out in rows of 100. Over the past year, each has endured the same wet winter and long summer drought. Now, the different ways each tree responded to these challenges are being analysed in trials that could shape the future of apple growing – and the taste of cider – for decades to come.

Myrtle Farm is the home of Thatchers Cider, which this year had its earliest ever harvest in the company’s 122-year history. Yet the farm’s experimental orchard of 3,800 trees, where each 100-tree row produces a different apple variety, offers hope that – even as the climate emergency deepens – future harvests will become more consistent and predictable.

Two
title: Drought, early harvests and wet winters: can an experimental orchard save the UK’s cider industry?

author: David Hytner in Madrid
description:
‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics

Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2. The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before.

The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16
title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid

author: Isobel Lewis
description:
The fad for plant-based junk food has run its course, but restaurants reflecting the centuries-long history of this cuisine still thrive

Have you ever gone to make a restaurant reservation and been met with a Google Maps listing bearing that harbinger of doom: “Permanently closed”? It’s a pretty deflating feeling – and one the UK’s vegan population knows well. Over the past few years, many once-beloved, plant-based establishments have shut up shop or moved away from brick-and-mortar businesses, from The Allotment in Manchester to The Vurger Co, which had restaurants in London and Brighton. Each shuttering galvanises the vegan community into supporting their local spots. But they’re gutting too, and deeply felt by a group who see themselves more as an ethically motivated community than simply clientele.

The so-called sorry state of the vegan restaurant scene has been widely reported on (not least
title: The corporate boom in vegan food is dead. Long live real plant-based cooking | Isobel Lewis

author: Ed Aarons
description:
Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead

Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February, but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”.

Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training
title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta

author: The Secret Cricket Coach
description:
Cricket always celebrates sportsmanship and condemns cheating, but where exactly is the line between the two?

I once played in a one-day semi-final. We were in a very tight spot when I edged the ball to the keeper. I didn’t walk. The opposition couldn’t believe it. They crowded around me, furious, and I was getting plenty of abuse.

I managed to get a single and when I reached the other end the umpire said: “You didn’t nick that did you? You are a walker.” “Yep, that’s right,” I replied.

Continue reading...
title: I built a reputation as a ‘walker’ so I could cheat when it mattered most – and it worked | The Secret Cricket Coach

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Chief executive of supermarket says it is considering new projects after success of Dish podcast and YouTube channel

Waitrose is to expand its digital broadcasting portfolio after this year’s Christmas ad launch with Keira Knightley attracted more that 2 million viewers.

“There are not many brands that would command an appointment of you for six minutes on ITV to launch their Christmas ad and have 2.3 million people show up to watch,” said the supermarket’s chief executive, Tom Denyard.

Continue reading...
title: Waitrose to expand digital broadcasting after festive ad launch wins 2m views

author: Luke Harding and Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv
description:
Photos of bridge, built after 2014 annexation and viewed by Ukraine as illegal, suggest massive steel arch has fallen into water

Ukraine has critically damaged the Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia in an overnight missile attack, in what Ukrainian officials say is a symbolic blow to the Kremlin.

Footage showed a Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile seconds before it hit the road and railway crossing, followed by an explosion. The strike follows an earlier attack on Monday that targeted an arch across its central section.

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine critically damages Kerch bridge linking occupied Crimea with Russia

author: Ajit Niranjan
description:
Thorny divisions emerge as wide-ranging draft deal seeks to ‘draw out parties’ on areas of disagreement

There’s plenty to go through in the coming days beyond the key sticking points. As part of a complementary platform to the negotiations, Cop31 is organized into “thematic days” and Tuesday is slated for “Oceans, Seas, Nature and Land Use”.

Cop31 was dubbed a “Blue COP” in anticipation that there would be substantial actions taken on oceans and that ocean-based solutions could be worked into climate commitments. At the start of the summit Ocean Conservancy Vice President, Dr. Fatima Candance, pointed to this year’s mascot – a loggerhead turtle – as an important symbol for the work. “But symbolism alone won’t deliver the action we need,” she said, urging leaders to move from “pledges to projects”.

Continue reading...<
title: Cop31 live: first draft of agreement under pressure as climate negotiations enter final days

author: Niha Masih
description:
As tourism booms, three experienced female travellers give their take on how to make the most of travelling here

The 13th-century Persian scholar Zakariyya al-Qazwini never travelled to India. But he catalogued it in his famous work The Wonders of Creation and Rarities of Existence, which drew on accounts of a distant land filled with “rarities par excellence”. For al-Qazwini, as Helen Pfeifer writes in the London Review of Books, wonder was not an emotion but an intellectual method of making sense of the world and acquiring knowledge.

India has long occupied such a space in the global imagination, as a land of extraordinary riches; spirituality, customs, chaos and contradictions. This has shaped how the country is perceived from afar, but it can often flatten its complexities.
title: India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes

author: Anna Tims
description:
A recent £364 renewal quote suddenly increased to an extortionate £796

My car was involved in a minor no-fault accident. The other driver admitted responsibility and said they would pay for repairs without involving insurers. I informed my insurer, the AA, without making a claim. It had recently sent a renewal quote for £364, but after reporting the accident I was sent a revised figure of £796.86.

I was told by a call handler that any insurance company would do the same. However, they eventually lowered the quote to £452.31. This seems extortionate for a no-fault, no-claim prang.

Continue reading...
title: Simply telling the AA about my minor no-fault, no-claim prang doubled my insurance quote

author: Helen Clark
description:
AI systems can allow militaries to find and annihilate targets within seconds. A meaningful treaty must prioritise human control – and accountability

Militaries around the world are increasingly relying on artificial intelligence to find, track and annihilate targets. An upcoming conference in Geneva offers a chance to confront the gravest risks of AI-enabled warfare, ideally through a treaty to regulate autonomous weapons systems.

A strike that might have taken half an hour and required significant human consideration only a few years ago can now take minutes, or even seconds, with AI systems taking the lead if they meet a confidence threshold set by a human operator.

Helen Clark is former head of the UN Development Programme and former prime minister of New Zealand, and member of The Elders
title: Automated warfare is already here. Now governments must restrain it | Helen Clark

author: Gareth Roberts
description:
A new coach service between Holyhead in the north and Carmarthen in the south offers a thrilling glimpse of west Wales, from mountain peaks to pretty seafronts – and it knocks half an hour off the journey

As anyone who has ever tried to catch a train from north to south Wales will know, it’s quite the adventure, and by adventure, I mean chore. You leave Wales, dip into England and then back into Wales to complete the journey. The fastest “Marches” route, which includes stops in Chester, Crewe and Shrewsbury, takes about five and a half hours and costs about £105, depending on your ticket.

There are lots of reasons for this: mid-Wales has some challenging topography; the old rail networks, before the Beeching cuts, predominantly bled outwards, transporting slate, coal and steel to distant ports and markets. Last month, all that changed. Just not in the way you probably imagine.
title: Is this Britain’s most beautiful bus journey? The Welsh service that beats the train hands down

author: Jordyn Beazley
description:
So You Are placed eighth in race just two weeks ago and was put down after a severe bout of colic

The body of a horse that placed eighth in the Melbourne Cup two weeks ago and recently fell ill has been found dumped in skip bin in Sydney.

The horse So You Are, a five year old Gelding, was put down after it suffered from a severe bout from colic and was taken to hospital on Monday for surgery.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Disgusted by it’: body of Melbourne Cup race horse found dumped in Sydney skip bin

author: Tom McIlroy in Manila
description:
Organisers say up to 10,000 people could join the next round of demonstrations ahead of the US president’s arrival in Manila for the Asean summit

  • Asean and Apec summits – live updates

Hundreds of people have been arrested in heated demonstrations against Donald Trump in Manila, as authorities braced for more protests ahead of the US president’s arrival in the city for a leaders’ summit.

Organisers claim as many as 10,000 people will join protests against Trump in the Philippine capital on Tuesday, when he will attend the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit. The crowds are expected to try to walk to the summit site.

Continue reading...
title: Hundreds arrested in anti-Trump protests in Philippines amid anger over Iran war and AI pact

author: Phil Harrison, Priya Elan, Hollie Richardson, Graeme Virtue, Alexi Duggins and Simon Wardell
description:
This Storyville film talks to Peter Sichel, who fled Nazi Germany, then became the CIA’s first station chief in Berlin. Plus: Stacey & Joe go camping. Here’s what to watch this evening

10pm, BBC Four
Some people are blessed with interesting lives, others are cursed with them. It’s hard to say which category Peter Sichel falls into, but he lived quite a story and managed to tell it in this documentary, shortly before his death, aged 102. As a child, he fled Nazi Germany for the US. He later landed at the CIA and played a role in some of the late-20th century’s pivotal events. His critique of US foreign policy during that era is forensic and fascinating. Phil Harrison

Continue reading...
title: TV tonight: the extraordinary story of the Jewish refugee boy who became a CIA spy

author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
description:
A new analysis from some of the architects of the Vote Leave campaign is very selective with its figures

A new analysis from some of the architects of the Vote Leave campaign has claimed rejoining the EU would cost Britain £750m a week. How did they arrive at these figures – and are they any more reliable than the ones on the side of the bus?

Continue reading...
title: Is £750m a week the real cost of rejoining the EU – or the Brexit bus myth all over again?

author: Sally Weale Education correspondent
description:
‘This department helped make my family who we are,’ says Kadiatu Kanneh-Mason

As the mother of seven supremely talented young musicians, Kadiatu Kanneh-Mason is better placed than most to understand the value of a musical education.

Her children, including the renowned cellist Sheku Kanneh-Mason, all benefited from the rich musical opportunities on offer in the state schools of Nottingham, where they grew up, and enjoyed the support of the music department at their local university.

Continue reading...
title: Mother of renowned musicians ‘devastated’ by closure of department at Nottingham University

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Campaigners call for reopening of high-speed Eurostar stations and new infrastructure for London St Pancras

Britain should throw its weight behind international rail services to reset the UK-EU relationship, transport campaigners have urged the prime minister.

A coalition of groups has called on Andy Burnham to commit to reopening high-speed stations for Eurostar and other services in Kent, and to support new infrastructure for passengers at London St Pancras and for rail freight.

Continue reading...
title: Invest in international rail services to boost UK-EU reset, Burnham urged

author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
description:
Bringing the number not in education, employment or training down from a decade high will be tough. Here’s why

  • Alan Milburn urges Burnham to spend billions on ‘new deal’ for young people

Almost a million young people – one in eight – in the UK are not in education, employment or training (Neet).

Having reached the highest level in a decade, the government is seeking to bring that number down after the recommendations made in Alan Milburn’s landmark report.

Continue reading...
title: Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts

author: Pippa Crerar and Lisa O’Carroll
description:
Prime minister signals Labour could drop its Brexit red lines in major foreign policy speech

Britain’s global standing has diminished in the decade since Brexit, Andy Burnham has said, as he again signalled that Labour could drop its red lines on Europe in its next manifesto.

In a foreign policy speech, Burnham said that after a major Brussels summit this week he would begin new discussions with the EU about options for “our long-term relationship”.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham says Brexit has dramatically diminished Britain’s global standing

author: Associated Press
description:
• Los Angeles Chargers 23-20 Baltimore Ravens

  • Chargers had lost 11 games in a row back to last season

Justin Herbert and Omarion Hampton ran for first-half touchdowns, and the Los Angeles Chargers earned their first win of the season, manhandling Baltimore at the line of scrimmage in a 23-20 victory over the Ravens on Monday night.

“I respect those guys in that locker room so much, for sticking together, not pointing fingers,” said Herbert after the game. “It’s been a tough year … but the way they continue to show up to work, they’re true professionals and I’m honored to be part of it.”

Continue reading...
title: Los Angeles Chargers beat reeling Baltimore Ravens to get first win of season

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Ukraine again hits symbolic bridge linking occupied Crimea to Russia; Kyiv’s heating and water disrupted as North and South bridges struck. What we know on day 1,728

Ukraine struck a symbolic bridge that links the annexed Crimean peninsula to Russia for the second day in a row, after Moscow launched strikes on Kyiv’s bridges. Crimea’s Moscow-installed governor Sergey Aksyonov said on Tuesday that Ukrainian forces had struck the bridge and traffic had been suspended. On Monday, a Ukrainian drone crashed into one of the Kerch bridge’s arches. Ukraine says the bridge is a legitimate target for its armed forces, and has made at least two previous attempts to blow it up.

Russian strikes hit two major bridges in Kyiv late on Monday, pa
title: Ukraine war briefing: Crimea bridge attacked again after Russia strikes major Kyiv bridges
